SUG:K-PS2-2.cc_advanced: I can test a ramp or other tool, use my results to explain how it changes an object's speed or direction, and make it work better.
SUG:K-PS2-2.cc_at_target: I can look at test results to tell if my design, like a ramp, changes the speed or direction of an object as I wanted.
SUG:K-PS2-2.cc_approaching: I can test a ramp with a ball and say if the ball went faster or changed direction, with help.
SUG:K-PS2-2.cc_emerging: I can push a ball and show that it can go fast, slow, or turn.

SUG:K-PS3-1.cc_advanced: I can compare how warm different surfaces get in the sun, such as sand, water, and grass, and explain why.
SUG:K-PS3-1.cc_at_target: I can make observations to tell how sunlight changes Earth's surface, such as making sand or water warmer.
SUG:K-PS3-1.cc_approaching: I can touch things in the sun and in the shade and say which is warmer, with help.
SUG:K-PS3-1.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun makes things feel warm.

SUG:K-ESS2-2.cc_advanced: I can give several examples of how plants, animals, and people change their surroundings and explain my evidence.
SUG:K-ESS2-2.cc_at_target: I can use evidence to tell how plants and animals, including people, change the environment to meet their needs, like a bird building a nest.
SUG:K-ESS2-2.cc_approaching: I can give one example of an animal or person changing a place, using pictures and sentence frames.
SUG:K-ESS2-2.cc_emerging: I can point to pictures of animal homes, like nests and holes.

SUG:K-2-ETS1-2.cc_advanced: I can draw or build a model, label its parts, and explain how changing its shape would make it work better.
SUG:K-2-ETS1-2.cc_at_target: I can make a simple sketch, drawing, or model to show how the shape of an object helps it do its job.
SUG:K-2-ETS1-2.cc_approaching: I can draw an object and say what one part of its shape does, with help.
SUG:K-2-ETS1-2.cc_emerging: I can draw or build a simple object, with teacher support.

SUG:K-2-ETS1-3.cc_advanced: I can test two designs, record results in a chart, and explain which is stronger and why.
SUG:K-2-ETS1-3.cc_at_target: I can look at test results from two objects made to solve the same problem and compare what each does well and not well.
SUG:K-2-ETS1-3.cc_approaching: I can test two designs and say which one worked better, with help.
SUG:K-2-ETS1-3.cc_emerging: I can watch two designs being tested and point to the one that worked.

SUG:1-LS1-2.cc_advanced: I can compare parent and baby behaviors from several animals in books or videos and explain how each helps the baby survive.
SUG:1-LS1-2.cc_at_target: I can read texts and use media to find patterns in how parents and offspring behave to help the offspring survive.
SUG:1-LS1-2.cc_approaching: I can name one way an animal parent helps its baby, like feeding it, using a book with help.
SUG:1-LS1-2.cc_emerging: I can match baby animals to their parents in pictures.

SUG:1-PS4-1.cc_advanced: I can design my own test to show that vibrating things make sound and that sound can make things vibrate, and explain my results.
SUG:1-PS4-1.cc_at_target: I can plan and do investigations to show that vibrating materials make sound and that sound can make materials vibrate.
SUG:1-PS4-1.cc_approaching: I can feel or see a vibration when I pluck a string or tap a drum, with help.
SUG:1-PS4-1.cc_emerging: I can make sounds with objects, like tapping a drum.

SUG:1-PS4-2.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence why we cannot see in a dark room and how light lets us see, using a test I did.
SUG:1-PS4-2.cc_at_target: I can make observations to show that objects can be seen only when there is light.
SUG:1-PS4-2.cc_approaching: I can look in a dark box and say I can see the object only when light shines in, with help.
SUG:1-PS4-2.cc_emerging: I can say that I need light to see.

SUG:1-PS4-3.cc_advanced: I can predict and test how clear, see-through, solid, and mirror materials change a light beam and explain the results.
SUG:1-PS4-3.cc_at_target: I can investigate what happens when different materials are put in the path of a beam of light.
SUG:1-PS4-3.cc_approaching: I can sort materials into ones that let light through and ones that block it, with help.
SUG:1-PS4-3.cc_emerging: I can shine a flashlight on objects and say what I see.

SUG:1-PS4-4.cc_advanced: I can build and improve a device that uses light or sound to send a message far away and explain how it works.
SUG:1-PS4-4.cc_at_target: I can use tools and materials to design and build a device that uses light or sound to communicate over a distance.
SUG:1-PS4-4.cc_approaching: I can build a simple device, like a cup phone or flashlight signal, by following steps with help.
SUG:1-PS4-4.cc_emerging: I can show a way to send a message, like waving or clapping.

SUG:1-ESS1-2.cc_advanced: I can compare daylight at different times of year and explain the pattern using my observations.
SUG:1-ESS1-2.cc_at_target: I can make observations at different times of year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year.
SUG:1-ESS1-2.cc_approaching: I can say whether it gets dark earlier or later in summer or winter, using a chart with help.
SUG:1-ESS1-2.cc_emerging: I can say when it is daytime and nighttime.

SUG:2-LS2-1.cc_advanced: I can design a fair test with plants and explain what my results show about light and water.
SUG:2-LS2-1.cc_at_target: I can plan and do an investigation to find out if plants need sunlight and water to grow.
SUG:2-LS2-1.cc_approaching: I can grow plants with and without water or light and say which grew better, with help.
SUG:2-LS2-1.cc_emerging: I can say that plants need water and sunlight.

SUG:2-LS2-2.cc_advanced: I can build a model of how an animal spreads seeds or pollen and explain how it helps the plant.
SUG:2-LS2-2.cc_at_target: I can make a simple model that works like an animal spreading seeds or pollinating plants.
SUG:2-LS2-2.cc_approaching: I can show with a model how a bee carries pollen or seeds stick to fur, with help.
SUG:2-LS2-2.cc_emerging: I can say that bees visit flowers.

SUG:2-LS4-1.cc_advanced: I can compare the variety of plants and animals in two habitats and explain why they are different.
SUG:2-LS4-1.cc_at_target: I can make observations of plants and animals to compare the diversity of life in different habitats.
SUG:2-LS4-1.cc_approaching: I can list plants and animals I see in one habitat, like the desert or the sea, with help.
SUG:2-LS4-1.cc_emerging: I can name some animals that live on land and in water.

SUG:2-PS1-1.cc_advanced: I can create my own groups for materials and explain the properties I used to sort them.
SUG:2-PS1-1.cc_at_target: I can investigate and classify different materials by their properties, like color, texture, hardness, and flexibility.
SUG:2-PS1-1.cc_approaching: I can sort materials as hard or soft, rough or smooth, with a word bank.
SUG:2-PS1-1.cc_emerging: I can name what an object is made of, like wood or plastic.

SUG:2-PS1-2.cc_advanced: I can test several materials and use the data to choose and justify the best one for a job.
SUG:2-PS1-2.cc_at_target: I can analyze test data to decide which materials have the best properties for a purpose.
SUG:2-PS1-2.cc_approaching: I can test two materials and say which is better for a job, like keeping water out, with help.
SUG:2-PS1-2.cc_emerging: I can say which material is good for a job, like a cup made of plastic.

SUG:2-PS1-3.cc_advanced: I can take apart an object made of pieces, build a new object, and explain how the same pieces made something different.
SUG:2-PS1-3.cc_at_target: I can use observations to explain how an object made of small pieces can be taken apart and made into a new object.
SUG:2-PS1-3.cc_approaching: I can take apart a block tower and build something new, and say what I did, with help.
SUG:2-PS1-3.cc_emerging: I can put blocks together and take them apart.

SUG:2-PS1-4.cc_advanced: I can predict which heating or cooling changes can be reversed, test them, and argue with evidence.
SUG:2-PS1-4.cc_at_target: I can use evidence to argue that some changes caused by heating or cooling can be reversed and some cannot.
SUG:2-PS1-4.cc_approaching: I can sort changes, like melting ice and cooking an egg, into can or cannot change back, with help.
SUG:2-PS1-4.cc_emerging: I can say that ice melts when it gets warm.

SUG:2-ESS1-1.cc_advanced: I can compare fast and slow Earth events from several sources and explain how long each takes to change the land.
SUG:2-ESS1-1.cc_at_target: I can use information from several sources to show that Earth events can happen quickly or slowly.
SUG:2-ESS1-1.cc_approaching: I can sort events, like an earthquake and erosion, into fast or slow, using pictures with help.
SUG:2-ESS1-1.cc_emerging: I can name an event that changes the land, like a flood.

SUG:2-ESS2-1.cc_advanced: I can test and compare designs that stop wind or water from moving sand and explain which works best.
SUG:2-ESS2-1.cc_at_target: I can compare different solutions that slow or stop wind or water from changing the shape of the land.
SUG:2-ESS2-1.cc_approaching: I can test one way to stop water from washing sand away and say if it worked, with help.
SUG:2-ESS2-1.cc_emerging: I can show that water and wind can move sand.

SUG:2-ESS2-2.cc_advanced: I can make a detailed model or map of land and water in an area and explain what it shows.
SUG:2-ESS2-2.cc_at_target: I can make a model to show the shapes and kinds of land and bodies of water in an area.
SUG:2-ESS2-2.cc_approaching: I can label land and water features, like hills and the sea, on a model with help.
SUG:2-ESS2-2.cc_emerging: I can point to land and water on a map or picture.

SUG:2-ESS2-3.cc_advanced: I can find where water is on Earth in different forms and explain which places have solid or liquid water.
SUG:2-ESS2-3.cc_at_target: I can get information to tell where water is found on Earth and that it can be solid or liquid.
SUG:2-ESS2-3.cc_approaching: I can name places with water, like oceans and ice, using pictures with help.
SUG:2-ESS2-3.cc_emerging: I can say that water can be ice or liquid.

SUG:3-PS2-4.cc_advanced: I can define a magnet design problem with clear criteria and constraints and explain how magnet ideas help solve it.
SUG:3-PS2-4.cc_at_target: I can define a simple design problem that can be solved using what I know about magnets.
SUG:3-PS2-4.cc_approaching: I can describe a problem a magnet could solve, like keeping a door closed, with a template.
SUG:3-PS2-4.cc_emerging: I can show that a magnet sticks to some objects.
